dedupe_keys.name: bikenodeplanner bicycle node network planning tool for qgis

description: BikeNodePlanner is an open-source decision support tool for planning bicycle node networks, the numbered signpost wayfinding systems for recreational and rural cycling that run along existing roads and paths. It was developed by Anastassia Vybornova, Ane Rahbek Vierø and Michael Szell at the IT University of Copenhagen with Kirsten Krogh Hansen of the Danish coastal and nature tourism organisation, and described in a 2024 arXiv paper. It is a set of modular Python scripts run inside QGIS: the user loads a proposed node network and context layers, and the tool evaluates and compares plans with metrics on land use along links, proximity to points of interest, elevation and slope, and network structure. Coverage is any region; a companion repository supplies prepared input data for Denmark, where it was used for the national node network. Access: code and documentation on GitHub. Licence and cost: GPL-3.0, free (the paper is CC BY-NC-SA). Caveats: it evaluates candidate networks, not generating optimal ones, demand and traffic safety are not modelled, and outside Denmark the user must prepare inputs. It supports capacity and network planning for cycling infrastructure. It complements the PeopleForBikes network analysis, the Sustrans National Cycle Network and OpenStreetMap records in the catalogue.
